open_questions: When was cefalexin first prescribed, and what was the indication?
What symptoms or signs were present before the cefalexin dose that led to its prescription?
Was an alternative antibiotic started after cefalexin was stopped due to allergy?
Was epinephrine, antihistamine, or corticosteroid administered for the lip swelling reaction?
Was the cefalexin allergy confirmed with testing or documented as patient-reported vs. observed?
Were any follow-up actions ordered after the allergic reaction (e.g., allergist referral, EpiPen prescription)?

candidate_highlights.risk_reason: Cefalexin allergy with objective sign (lip swelling) indicates a potentially serious hypersensitivity reaction; re-exposure risk remains if not fully mitigated.
candidate_highlights.suggested_action: Verify current medication list excludes all cephalosporins and cross-reactive antibiotics; confirm allergy is formally documented in problem list and pharmacy system.
